# Provenance of the vendored CLI11.hpp

`CLI11.hpp` in this directory is a single-header build of
[CLI11](https://github.com/CLIUtils/CLI11), a header-only C++11(+) command-line
parsing library. It provides every `CLI::App`/`add_option`/`add_flag` call
`src/cli_main.cpp` makes; conduitscope does not implement any CLI-parsing
logic of its own.

## What's vendored, and why

Only the generated single-include header is kept here -- not a full CLI11
checkout, not the multi-header `include/CLI/` source tree upstream builds it
from, and not CLI11's own tests/docs/build scripts. `CMakeLists.txt` adds this
directory straight to `conduitscope`'s include path (see the comment above
`target_include_directories(conduitscope PRIVATE ".../third_party/CLI11")`),
so `src/cli_main.cpp`'s `#include <CLI11.hpp>` resolves directly against
this one file. That's
deliberate: it's what keeps conduitscope's stated "zero required
dependencies, just a C++17 compiler and CMake" build promise true on both
Linux and Windows (see `README.md`'s BUILDING section) -- no vcpkg/Conan/apt
package, no submodule, nothing to fetch at configure time.

## Version and upstream source

- **Version vendored:** 2.4.2, released 2024-05-04.
- **Upstream repository:** <https://github.com/CLIUtils/CLI11>
- **Upstream tag:** [`v2.4.2`](https://github.com/CLIUtils/CLI11/releases/tag/v2.4.2)
- **How this exact file is produced upstream:** CLI11 is authored as a normal
  multi-header library under `include/CLI/`; the single file here is generated
  from that source by CLI11's own `scripts/MakeSingleHeader.py`, run against a
  released tag. The generated file states this itself in its own header
  comment (`CLI11.hpp` lines 1-9): "This is a standalone header file
  generated by MakeSingleHeader.py in CLI11/scripts from: v2.4.2". This
  repository did not modify the generated output in any way after pulling it
  in -- it's byte-identical to what that tag produces (or to the
  identical asset CLI11 attaches to its GitHub release; see below).
- **License:** 3-clause BSD, embedded verbatim in the file's own header
  comment (`CLI11.hpp` lines 1-30) -- Copyright (c) 2017-2024 University of
  Cincinnati, developed by Henry Schreiner under NSF AWARD 1414736. That
  license is compatible with conduitscope's own Apache-2.0 license (see the
  repository root `LICENSE`); no separate `NOTICE` entry is needed beyond
  what's already inline in the vendored file itself.

## How to check whether this has fallen behind upstream

1. Compare the version this file states against upstream's latest release:
   <https://github.com/CLIUtils/CLI11/releases>. (At the time this note was
   written, `v2.5.0` was upstream's latest tag -- newer than the `v2.4.2`
   vendored here. That gap is not itself urgent: CLI11 is a mature, stable
   parser and conduitscope uses a fairly narrow slice of its API, so there's
   no standing obligation to track every release. Update when a specific
   upstream fix/feature is wanted, or periodically as routine maintenance --
   not reflexively on every tag.)
2. Skim that release's changelog for anything relevant to how conduitscope
   actually uses CLI11 (`add_option`/`add_flag`/subcommands/validators in
   `src/cli_main.cpp` -- grep there for `CLI::` and `->` chains to see the
   surface actually exercised).

## How to update

1. Get the new version's single-include header. Either:
   - Download the `CLI11.hpp` asset attached directly to the desired release
     on <https://github.com/CLIUtils/CLI11/releases> (upstream publishes a
     pre-built single-include header per release, meant for exactly this
     kind of vendoring), or
   - Build it yourself: clone CLI11 at the desired tag, configure with
     `-DCLI11_SINGLE_FILE=ON` (the default; needs Python 3 on the `PATH`,
     no other dependencies), and the generated file appears at
     `<build-dir>/single-include-generated/CLI11.hpp` (or run
     `python3 scripts/MakeSingleHeader.py` directly from a CLI11 checkout).
2. Replace this directory's `CLI11.hpp` with the new one. Confirm the new
   file's own header comment (lines 1-9) states the version/tag you expect --
   that's the vendored copy's own provenance record, so it should always be
   read back after an update, not just written once here.
3. Rebuild across this project's three established configs (default +
   libpcap, `-DCONDUITSCOPE_ENABLE_LIVE_CAPTURE=OFF`, MinGW cross-compile --
   see `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`'s verification conventions) with zero new
   warnings, then run the full `ctest` suite. CLI11 is used narrowly enough
   here (basic options/flags/subcommands, no exotic validators) that a
   version bump within the same major version should be behavior-preserving,
   but this project's own CLI-surface tests
   (`resource_limit_flags_present_in_*_help` and friends in `CMakeLists.txt`,
   plus every `--help`/argument-parsing-adjacent test) are what actually
   confirm that for conduitscope's specific usage, not an assumption from
   CLI11's own changelog.
4. Update the "Version vendored" line (and the tag/date) above in this same
   commit -- this file is the record that's supposed to stay in sync, so an
   update that doesn't touch it isn't finished.

See `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`'s "External code review and engineering
priorities" item 8 for why this file exists.
